clue.text: A Catholic, hit hard, gets a big shiner

parts.note: RC is the usual abbreviation for Roman Catholic
to lamp someone is British slang for punching them hard

explanation.surface: A Catholic who has been punched hard ends up with a huge black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shiner' looks like a black eye from the punch, but here it means something that shines. LAMP is British slang for hitting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp gives off a very bright light, so it is a large source of light, something that shines.

clue.text: I am old model, overwhelmed by some strong hostility

indicators.note: something overwhelmed by another thing is engulfed by it, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'is there any left?'
I'm is the short form of I am
to sit is to pose as a model does for an artist

explanation.surface: An older model complains of being swamped by fierce dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity is deep ill will or enmity, a forceful dislike.

clue.text: Part of article mentioned Freud, for one

indicators.note: part of says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A piece of writing referred to the psychoanalyst Sigmund Freud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freud' suggests Sigmund, but the definition is his grandson Clement Freud, a British broadcaster and politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Freud was a British writer, broadcaster and MP, so Freud is an example of someone with this first name.

clue.text: Gather church service is led by archbishop principally

indicators.note: something led by another comes after it, so that letter goes in front
principally means chiefly or first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: Mass is the service of the Eucharist in the Catholic church

explanation.surface: People gather for a church service led by an archbishop.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Official documents: one's disregarded by people in hospital

indicators.note: something disregarded is left out, so this letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: patients are people being treated in hospital
one is I, the Roman numeral, with 's standing for is

explanation.surface: Hospital patients ignore some formal paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Patents are official government documents granting rights to an invention.

clue.text: To some extent, political group can enlist Liberal

indicators.note: a party that enlists someone takes them into its ranks, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a party is a political group

explanation.surface: A political party is allowed to recruit a Liberal member.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning in part, not completely.

clue.text: Fish — brill — served about noon maybe

parts.note: a perch is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: brill and ace are both slang for excellent
N is short for noon, twelve o'clock

explanation.surface: Brill, a flatfish, might be served at lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brill' looks like the fish, but here it is British slang for brilliant; 'served' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an old-fashioned word for perhaps.

clue.text: Burden of brother in control

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second

parts.note: to rein in is to control, and a rein is a means of control
Fra is the Italian title for a friar, meaning brother, as in Fra Angelico

explanation.surface: A brother is weighed down with the responsibility of being in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burden' suggests a load, but it also means the chorus of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden in music is the recurring chorus of a song, the part that repeats.

clue.text: Organ prelude not used in stage musical

indicators.note: the prelude is the opening part, so dropping it removes the first letter

parts.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's stage musical based on Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: A church organ's opening music is left out of a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' and 'prelude' suggest music, but the organ is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver is an organ of the body that processes blood.

clue.text: During part of year, I wonder about becoming member of restaurant staff

indicators.note: something happening during a season sits inside it, so the other letters go into the middle of the season's name

parts.note: winter is one season, a part of the year

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the words I and wonder round and read them backwards

parts.note: awe is a feeling of wonder

explanation.surface: Someone in midwinter wonders about the job they are taking on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During part of year' reads as a time phrase, but the season's name is the container; 'about' turns I AWE round to EWAI, and 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine waiter, or sommelier, is the restaurant employee who serves the wine.

clue.text: Much-loved female Roman's greeting

parts.note: ave is the Latin word Romans used to say hail

explanation.surface: A Roman woman is warmly greeted by those who adore her.
explanation.definitionFit: Fave is informal for favourite, the one that is loved best.

clue.text: Here a violinist performed 70s' disco hit

indicators.note: a piece of music that is performed is played out, here showing the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A violinist played here, performing a well-known disco record of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of John Paul Young's 1977 disco single, a big hit of that decade.

clue.text: Gave misleading information about paper being stolen

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: lied means told untruths, gave false information
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone told lies about a newspaper being stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is informal for to steal it, so lifted is a synonym for taken illegally.

clue.text: Find night club jolly

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub for dancing
jolly is British informal for very, as in jolly good

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a nightclub full of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective for cheerful, but in British usage it also means very.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is something found, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Family man hammering nails now

indicators.note: hammering beats something out of shape, here showing the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A family man is busy knocking nails in right now.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter's husband becomes a relative by marriage, a male member of the family.

clue.text: Help to suppress charge over the illegal segregation of races

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down within, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: over tells us to turn the word for charge round

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap

explanation.surface: Assistance is used to cover up a charge over illegal racial segregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns RAP back to PAR. A rap is American slang for a criminal charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was South Africa's system of racial segregation, now outlawed and condemned internationally.

clue.text: Gay man is exercising in these?

definitions.text: Gay man is exercising in these?

indicators.note: exercising suggests vigorous movement, so the letters are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about where a cheerful man goes to work out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: a man exercising would be found in these places.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnasia is the Latin-style plural of gymnasium, halls where people exercise.

clue.text: What antiperspirant guarantees without a quibble?

definitions.meaning: a product that stops perspiration promises its user stays dry
an informal phrase for easily, no trouble at all

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means no perspiration and is idiomatic for no problem or easily done.

clue.text: Another rookie teacher's just starting to take over class? That could be novel

indicators.note: one piece taking over from another comes before it, so these letters go in front
just starting means only the opening letter of each of these words is used

parts.note: a form is a class in a British school

explanation.surface: Another new teacher is only just beginning to take charge of a class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but here it is a noun, a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel is one genre of creative work, so a novel is an example of this category.

clue.text: Catch close colleague finishing early, retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters are read backwards
something finishing early stops before its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a partner is a close colleague in business

explanation.surface: A close colleague who clocks off early is caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' cuts PARTNER to PARTNE, and 'retiring' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to catch them in a trap or by trickery, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Hard work making road round Virginia

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a trail is a track or path, a kind of road
VA is the US state abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: Building a road around Virginia is laborious.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful or laborious effort, toil.

clue.text: A protestant boy coming to grief in transatlantic conflict

indicators.note: something that comes to grief is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Protestant lad gets into trouble in a war across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1773 protest in Boston against British taxes on tea was a clash between American colonists and Britain across the ocean.

clue.text: Two billion people

parts.note: a race is a people, an ethnic group

explanation.surface: The world's population numbered two billion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' looks like part of the number, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a pair, as in a brace of pheasants.

clue.text: Leading man in a commercial

indicators.note: in puts the word for man inside the other letters

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, an advertisement
he is a pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: The star actor appears in a television advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading man' looks like one phrase, but 'Leading' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead means in front, in the lead.

clue.text: Ordered World War II pilot to offer no resistance

indicators.note: to offer no resistance means the resistance is absent, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: Douglas Bader was a famous RAF fighter pilot of the Second World War
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A wartime pilot is commanded not to fight back.
explanation.definitionFit: Bade is the past tense of bid, meaning commanded or told someone to do something.

clue.text: Old individual judged and given a pardon

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
one is a single person, an individual
rated means assessed or judged

explanation.surface: An old person is tried in court and then pardoned.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exonerated is to be cleared of blame, freed from guilt as a pardon does.

clue.text: Dope and crack for the aristocracy

parts.note: gen and dope are both slang for information
to have a crack at something is to have a try

explanation.surface: Drugs and crack cocaine are supplied to upper-class users.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' and 'crack' look like drugs; here they mean information and an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are people of high social rank, the class just below or alongside the nobility.

clue.text: Confused religious scholar carried by beast of burden, with daughter on the back

indicators.note: on the back means added at the end, so this letter follows the rest
something carried by an animal sits on or within it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a mule is used to carry loads
DD stands for Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A bewildered theologian rides a mule with his daughter riding behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddled means mixed up or bewildered in thought.
